senses.gloss: m. (πάτρικος, patricus, -a, -um) something hereditary, heirloom, patrimony. Y’lamd. to Num. XXI, 1, quot. in Ar. יודעין אנו שיש להן מאבותיהן פטריקא וכ׳ we know that they (Israel) have a legacy from their ancestors who said to them, ‘the voice is Jacob’s voice’ (i.e. prayer); I, too, rely on my patrimony, as it is said (Gen. XXVII, 40), ‘by thy sword thou shalt live’; Yalk. Num. 764.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 49:2">Gen. R. s. 49</cite> <he>אילו מפ׳ שלו וכ׳</he> if I asked (permission to cut some trees down) on his patrimony, he would not refuse me.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 98:6">Gen. R. s. 98</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 49:8">Gen. XLIX, 8</cite>, a.

<cite ref="II Samuel 22:41">II Sam. XXII, 41</cite>) <he>שהיה פ׳ שלו וכ׳</he> (not <he>שהיו פטיריקין</he>) it was his (Judah’s) hereditary privilege (paternal blessing, to lay hands on the enemy’s neck); <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:32">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 41</cite> <cite ref="Q00433"><he>פזמריקון</he></cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 162">Yalk. Gen. 162</cite> <he>פזמיקון</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 163">Yalk. Sam. 163</cite> <cite ref="Q00610"><he>פיזמיקון</he></cite> (corr. acc.).—Pl. <cite ref="Q00560"><he>פַּטְרִיקִין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 766:3">Yalk. Num. 766</cite> <he>שתי פ׳ של ברכות וכ׳</he> they have two paternal blessings from Aram.
